conviction_note: Mixed, mostly-priced evidence. The company already guided Networks sales above seasonality and Networks gross margin at 48-50%, consensus (+6% QoQ Networks vs +1% seasonal) already sits on that guide, and the 4Q26 memory-cost series points to more gross-margin pressure in the Q4 outlook. Against that, ADR short interest is building (DTC 10.2), the stock is 5.6% off its 52-week low after a -12.6% Q2 reaction, and the inventory build and Transsion IPR support delivery. abs_move is held at the option-implied ~8.5% and p_up near 50; the two measurements agree that the direction is close to a coin flip.
bar: Infront consensus compiled 2026-10-08 from 16 analysts: net sales SEK 55.4bn (Networks 35.1bn, Cloud Software & Services 15.2bn, Enterprise 4.7bn), adj gross margin 47.3%, adj EBITA SEK 7.9bn (14.2%) (https://hurbra.se/ericsson-rapport-q3-2026-infor/, 2026-10-12). This agrees with Ericsson's own post-Q2 Infront file (2026-07-27, 15 contributors: sales ~SEK 55.5bn, EBITA ~7.9bn) and its current-quarter data page (Networks consensus +6% QoQ vs company guide 'above 3-year average seasonality' of +1%; CSS +3%; https://www.ericsson.com/en/investors/financial-reports-and-presentations/current-quarter-data-points). Company guide: Networks adj gross margin 48-50% for Q3 (pre-guide Infront 49.7%, https://www.placera.se/telegram/ericsson-spar-just-bruttomarg-networks-48-50-3-kv-est-49-7-20260714). Bar sourced to the company guide and two agreeing estimate sources, so sizes are not capped.
positioning_check: ADR (ERIC) short interest 74.78M shares at 2026-09-30 settlement, up from 64.53M at 09-15 and 61.55M at 08-14; days to cover 10.21, up from 8.24 and the highest in the eight settlements shown; 2.3% of total shares (https://equibles.com/stocks/eric/shortinterest, read 2026-10-14). Swedish FI register for ERIC B not checked. Baseline: 25-delta skew null (not available); put/call open-interest ratio 0.31 (call-heavy); front-expiry event-implied move 8.63%; ATM spread 18% of mid. Tape: -3.64% over 20 days, +2.17% over 5 days, -29.7% from the 52-week high, +5.6% above the 52-week low. Ericsson is buying back its own B shares: SEK 746m in the week of 5-9 Oct 2026 at an average SEK 94.27.

findings.finding: In Q2, inventory rose from SEK 25.7bn to 30.7bn and cut free cash flow to SEK 0.4bn. Ericsson attributed the build to deliveries planned for Q3, and it guided Q3 Networks sales growth above 3-year seasonality (+1%). That supports consensus of +6% QoQ for Networks (SEK 35.1bn) being delivered, with an inventory unwind and better Q3 cash flow. The preview names cash flow and inventory as the strongest signal for the stock.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: sales missed by about 2% (IPR and the timing of India deliveries, per Jefferies). Shares fell 12.6% in Stockholm and about 13.5% for the ADR, although adj EBITA beat by 3%. Q1 2026 (17 Apr): sales and profit slightly below expectations, shares down about 4-5%. Ålandsbanken: a 'normal' Ericsson report day is about ±7%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus is already +6% QoQ against a +1% seasonal norm, so the sales delivery is mostly in the bar. What may not be priced is the cash and inventory unwind: Q2 FCF was SEK 0.4bn, and if the market expected a strong Q3 FCF rebound, the stock would not be sitting 5.6% off its 52-week low.
findings.independence: This shares the company's Q2 statement with the guidance on the Ericsson data page (https://www.ericsson.com/en/investors/financial-reports-and-presentations/current-quarter-data-points). It lands inside what the company already guided.

findings.finding: Currency is neutral to the bar. Actual Q3 USD/SEK averaged 9.61 against Ericsson's outlook assumption of 9.7, and EUR/SEK 11.07 against 11.0. Ericsson estimates the Q3 currency impact at about 0% YoY and +2% QoQ, and about 0% since the Q2 reporting date, so there is no FX surprise to sales versus models built after July.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026, FX cut reported sales by about SEK 1.8bn and contributed to the reported miss, which the market sold.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: the company published it. It is filed so a judge knows FX is not a source of surprise this quarter, unlike Q2.
findings.independence: The HurBra preview also expects a roughly neutral YoY currency effect: https://hurbra.se/ericsson-rapport-q3-2026-infor/

findings.finding: Memory-cost inflation has not peaked. On 2026-09-30 TrendForce forecast 4Q26 conventional DRAM contract prices up another 10-15% QoQ (15-20% including HBM) and NAND up 15-20%, after 13-18% in 3Q26. Ericsson said in July that the component-cost impact 'builds in the coming quarters', and Citi called the margin pressure extending into 2027 the bigger concern. The Q4 Networks gross-margin outlook is therefore at risk of a weaker guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: the component-cost flag plus a Q3 Networks gross-margin guide about 2% below Morgan Stanley's expected Networks gross profit were the main reason the stock fell about 13% (zerohedge/Placera). Q1 2026: semiconductor input costs were cited, and the stock fell about 4-5%.
findings.why_not_priced: The company flagged the direction in July and the stock reset on it, so the direction is partly priced. What is new is that a fresh industry series shows prices still rising double digits into Q4, rather than easing as Ericsson's pricing actions would need. If the market had fully priced a weaker Q4 margin guide, the July consensus EBITA margin path would have been cut; Q3 consensus EBITA is unchanged at SEK 7.9bn since July 27.
findings.independence: This is a proxy: an industry price series, not an Ericsson number. Citi's July comment (https://placera.se/nyheter/det-sager-analytikerna-om-ericssons-rapport-2026-07-14) and the Q2 CEO statement (https://www.ericsson.com/en/press-releases/2026/7/ericsson-reports-second-quarter-results-2026) point the same way but predate the series.

findings.finding: Dell'Oro (2026-08-18) said the RAN market grew YoY for a third consecutive quarter in 2Q26, but that Ericsson's results were 'softer than expected' while Huawei had a strong quarter, and it kept full-year 2026 RAN flat. Nokia's Q2 radio networks grew 7% YoY, while Ericsson Networks fell about 4% organically (roughly flat excluding IPR). That is a share and relative-momentum question for Q3 Networks sales.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: Networks was the weak spot (Morgan Stanley), and the stock fell 12.6% in Stockholm.
findings.why_not_priced: These are Q2 data and largely priced in the July drawdown. Kept small because a flat 2026 RAN market and a share-losing Q2 do not fit easily with consensus +6% QoQ Networks growth. If the market believed the gap had closed, the stock would not be back below its post-Q2 low.

findings.finding: ADR short interest rose into the print: 74.78M shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, against 64.53M on 09-15 and 61.55M on 08-14 (+21% in six weeks). Days to cover is 10.21, the highest in the eight settlements listed. Call-heavy open interest (put/call OI 0.31) sits on the other side. A clean or in-line print has a covering mechanism in the US session.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved record for this name on positioning. In Q4 2025 (Jan 2026), a beat with a SEK 15bn buyback rallied strongly (Handelsbanken expected +5-8%).
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is published with a lag and is not in any preview read. At 2.3% of total shares it is not crowded as a share of shares, so the squeeze mechanism is modest. Some ADR shorts may be arbitrage against Stockholm, which caps the size.
findings.independence: Baseline put/call open-interest ratio 0.31 (sealed baseline, Yahoo options). There is no other independent source.

findings.finding: The SEK 15bn buyback (2026-04-23 to 2027-03-31) is running at about SEK 0.75bn a week: 7.92M B shares bought on 5-9 Oct 2026 at an average SEK 94.27. Treasury shares stand at 125.8M against 38.0M before the program, so roughly 88M shares and about SEK 8bn have been bought, leaving about SEK 7bn to buy through March. That is a steady bid under the stock after the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 (Jan 2026): the buyback announcement was part of a strong positive reaction. There is no history of the stock reacting to buyback progress.
findings.why_not_priced: The program is public, so it is mostly priced. What is filed is the pace: weekly purchases equal several percent of Stockholm B-share turnover, which is a mechanical bid if the print disappoints.
findings.independence: Share counts on Ericsson's data page (treasury 105.7M at 2026-09-04): https://www.ericsson.com/en/investors/financial-reports-and-presentations/current-quarter-data-points

findings.finding: This is the first report under CEO Per Narvinger, in post since 2026-10-01 and previously head of Networks. A new CEO's first report carries reset risk on targets, restructuring and outlook. Consensus FY26 restructuring is SEK -5.5bn, which the company calls 'elevated', and 1,600 Swedish job cuts were noticed in January 2026. Coverage frames the appointment as continuity, which lowers but does not remove the risk of a kitchen-sink outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No previous Ericsson print under a new CEO is in the window considered. Restructuring is excluded from adjusted EBITA, which the stock trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: This is an inference, not a document. If the market expected a reset, the implied move would be wider than about 8.6% against a recent print of -12.6%. It is filed small because Narvinger ran Networks and coverage reads continuity.
findings.independence: Restructuring consensus and 'elevated' language: https://www.ericsson.com/en/investors/financial-reports-and-presentations/current-quarter-data-points. Sweden notice of 1,600: https://apps.eurofound.europa.eu/restructuring-events/detail/203969

findings.finding: In July 2026 Ericsson signed IPR licenses with a top-10 smartphone vendor (Transsion, per the preview) and a payment-terminal vendor, lifting annualised recurring IPR to about SEK 13.5bn. The Transsion effect is expected from Q3. That compares with SEK 3.4bn of IPR in Q2 and 3.1bn in Q1, and lower IPR was the main cause of Q2's sales miss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: the sales miss was attributed mainly to lower IPR, and the stock fell 12.6%. IPR drops almost entirely to EBITA, so a beat or miss on it moves the profit line.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-rate is company-published, so models should carry it. The open question is a possible catch-up payment in the first recognising quarter, which is not in the annualised figure. Filed small because it lands inside what the company communicated.
findings.independence: The HurBra preview says the Transsion license effect is expected from Q3: https://hurbra.se/ericsson-rapport-q3-2026-infor/

baseline_tension: There is no skew number to cut against. The 20-day run-up is negative and the stock is near its 52-week low after the -12.6% Q2 reaction, so low expectations and rising ADR shorts lean slightly positive. The guided Networks margin pressure and continued memory inflation are known negatives, so the evidence is balanced and the option-implied ~8.6% is kept as the scale.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (inside the guide): the inventory and Networks-delivery finding lands inside the company's 'above seasonality' guide, so it was cut from +0.8 to +0.5.
Lesson 6 (inside the guide) and lesson 5 (proxy): memory-cost inflation was already flagged by the company and the finding rests on an industry series, so it was cut from -1.0 to -0.7.
Lesson 7 (positioning): ADR short interest is building but only 2.3% of total shares and partly ADR arbitrage, so the positioning finding was cut from +0.8 to +0.6.
Lesson 6 (inside what was communicated): the Transsion IPR run-rate is company-published, so the finding was cut from +0.4 to +0.2; the buyback, already public, was cut from +0.3 to +0.2.

Final lesson (untrustworthy history): the base rate was rebuilt from confirmed prints (Q1 2026 about -4-5%, Q2 2026 -12.6% Stockholm, Ålandsbanken ±7% 'normal') and the 6-K-based history was ignored. abs_move_pct was kept at 8.5 and not shrunk; p_up moved from 52 to 51.
